slides.alt: A chain link for joining ideas
slides.hint: Mei lost her bag. She asked the teacher for help. The second part shows the result.
slides.notes: SET INDUCTION (~4 min, silent think + whisper). Sayable: Yesterday you picked the missing sentence. Today the sentence is there. One word inside is wrong. You swap that one word. Point at headline, then reveal hint as recall of Bridge/result language.
slides.prompt: Yesterday we joined sentences. Today we repair words.

slides.feedback: went fits yesterday. go is present, so time breaks.
slides.hint: Find the time word. It says when.
slides.notes: MODEL 1 (~5 min, full think-aloud). Cover the sentence, show only go goes to went; everything else stays identical. Sayable: One word out. One word in. Nothing else moves. Corrects spelling-rewrite reflex.
slides.prompt: Point at the wrong word. Pick the fix.
slides.sentence: Yesterday Amir {{blank}} to the library with his sister. They borrowed two storybooks about animals.

slides.feedback: at pairs with arrived. at early morning is three words, so no mark.
slides.hint: Count the words you change. P1P2 allows one.
slides.notes: MODEL 2 (~4 min). Say the broken version aloud first: arrived to school. B sounds longer and better but has a space in it, so it scores zero. Sayable: If your answer has a space, it is two words. One box, one word.
slides.prompt: Pick the one word that repairs it.
slides.sentence: On Saturday we arrived {{blank}} school at seven for training.

slides.feedback: but shows contrast. because gives a reason, which breaks meaning.
slides.hint: Tired, yet he still joined. Twist or reason?
slides.notes: GUIDED 1 conjunction (~4 min, silent finger 1/2 + whisper). Redirect verb-tense reflex: did any verb change? No. The verbs are fine. The join is wrong. Whisper cue: twist or reason?
slides.prompt: Pick the one word that repairs it.
slides.sentence: Hakim felt tired {{blank}} he joined football training after school.

slides.feedback: at pairs with arrived. to fits go, not arrived here.
slides.hint: Say it with arrived: arrived ___ the canteen.
slides.notes: GUIDED 2 preposition (~4 min). L1 transfer sampai ke makes to tempting. Force the verb test: cover the rest, say arrived at / arrived to aloud. Sayable: the verb before decides the small word after.
slides.prompt: Pick the one word that repairs it.
slides.sentence: On Saturday we arrived {{blank}} the canteen at seven.

slides.feedback: watched fits Last night. watches is present, so time breaks.
slides.hint: Find the time word at the start.
slides.notes: GUIDED 3 verb (~4 min). Watch for pupils fixing night to nights instead of the verb. Redirect: spelling is fine, grammar time is broken. Follow-up: name the frame, past narrative.
slides.prompt: Pick the one word that repairs it.
slides.sentence: Last night Ali {{blank}} a football match with his family.

slides.feedback: glasses matches two. glass is one, so number breaks.
slides.hint: How many? Two means more than one.
slides.notes: GUIDED 4 noun (~4 min). Counter sounds-fine: point at two, then at the noun. These two must agree. Whisper follow-up: show one finger or two, then point at the noun.
slides.prompt: Pick the one word that repairs it.
slides.sentence: She drank two {{blank}} of warm milk before school.

slides.feedback: She points to Sara. He points to a boy, so it breaks.
slides.hint: Who lost the bag? Point back.
slides.notes: GUIDED 5 pronoun (~3 min, fast transfer). Same check as yesterday: pronoun points to the sentence before. If split, ask boy or girl, then which word says that.
slides.prompt: Pick the one word that repairs it.
slides.sentence: Sara lost her bag. {{blank}} looked everywhere in the classroom.

slides.feedback: an fits a vowel sound. a fits consonants, not here.
slides.hint: Say it: a elephant. What sound starts elephant?
slides.notes: GUIDED 6 article (~3 min). Counter same-meaning: P1P2 tests small words too, one mark each. Transition: six families, let us put them on one card.
slides.prompt: Pick the one word that repairs it.
slides.sentence: We saw {{blank}} elephant at the zoo on our school trip.

slides.notes: SYNTHESIS (~3 min, reference only, no new teaching, no pending answer). Read aloud once, sayably. State: this card stays up; it is your toolkit, not a question. Keep visible or re-show during the two master challenges.
slides.text: 1 Joining word: but, not because. 2 Small word: at, not to. 3 Verb: went, not go. 4 Naming word: glasses, not glass. 5 Pointing word: she, not he. 6 a/an: an, not a.

slides.feedback: so shows the result. and only adds, the test wants the result word.
slides.hint: Joining word. Forgot, then what happened?
slides.notes: APPLY 1 (~5 min, silent notebook write, sample 2 voices, type one). Redirect verb reflex: verbs already match Last Saturday, check the join. Whisper: name the check first, then the word. Toolkit card stays up.
slides.prompt: Name the check. Say the one word.
slides.stimulus: Last Saturday Kumar cycled to school for practice. He forgot his water bottle, and he shared his friend's drink.

slides.feedback: its shows the plants belong to the garden. it alone cannot own.
slides.hint: Whose plants? Point at the owner.
slides.notes: APPLY 2 (~5 min). Common wrong answer the: sounds fine but loses whose; its keeps the owner. Counter any-small-word: point at the owner, which word carries it.
slides.prompt: Name the check. Say the one word.
slides.stimulus: Our school garden grows chillies and herbs. Each class waters it plants every morning before lessons.

slides.notes: EXIT EVIDENCE (~3 min, silent finger scan). Record which families get few fingers as the reteach target for worksheet day. Close sayable: one word out, one word in; name the check before you fix.
slides.prompt: Fingers up: which check saved you? 1 joining, 2 small word, 3 verb, 4 naming, 5 pointing, 6 a/an.

title: One Word Out, One Word In
